decision.detail: I walk past the ballroom doors without looking in. The light on the station line is green, open, waiting. I pull the reel out of my bag—the one, the only one, Alma's hands on the gate, her voice saying what she wants her daughter to know. I seat it in the transport. I thread the leader. I key the Pittsburgh number into the board, the way you'd dial a phone, three digits, two, three digits. I push transmit. The reel starts turning. I stand there and watch it go, watching the little counter tick, and when it stops I pull the leader, set the reel in its can, and set the can in my bag. The line clicks back to green. Done. Pittsburgh has it. I don't go to the ballroom. I don't open my notebook. I walk out the front door of the Rialto into the February cold and I don't look back at the lights.
decision.intention: Alma's voice reaches her daughter tonight. Tonight. Not Thursday. Not after the network decides what the story is. Tonight, on a reel that is one person's hands and one person's words, going to the one person who asked. That is the whole piece. I made it. I sent it. I am done.
decision.words: Nothing. Maybe, very low, to the green light on the line: "There you go, Alma. There you go."
